memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Erin chose Hotel Santa Fe over Drury Plaza for the Santa Fe weekend because quieter setting, easier parking, and recovery amenities outweighed the downtown walking advantage. She selected a refundable patio king if the rate stayed near $275/night, with Drury Plaza as the backup.

messages.content: Mark read the Santa Fe shortlist and is leaning quieter, as long as the total stays close. Can you rerun Hotel Santa Fe versus Drury Plaza for the three nights with parking and fees? I also want to know if the balcony or patio request changes the answer.

Using Fri Mar 13 to Mon Mar 16 and refundable rates, I’d frame it this way: Drury Plaza is the easy restaurant/walkable pick: balcony king about $294/night, taxes and fees around $155, parking about $105, so roughly $1,140 total. Hotel Santa Fe is the quieter recovery pick: standard king about $252/night or patio king about $275/night, taxes/fees around $145-$155, parking about $45, so roughly $955 standard or $1,025 patio. Drury wins for park-once-and-walk dinners. Hotel Santa Fe wins on quieter feel, easier parking, and the pool/hot tub/fitness combination.
Does Drury’s breakfast and evening food erase much of that premium? We’d use breakfast, probably not the evening thing.

It helps, but it probably doesn’t erase it. If you value breakfast at $20-$25 per person per day, Drury gives back maybe $120-$150 over the weekend. Since you’d skip most evening food, the real premium after breakfast savings is closer to $0-$60 versus Hotel Santa Fe patio, or about $80-$130 versus the standard king. The trade is less about pure dollars and more about whether downtown convenience is worth the tighter parking and busier setting.
Least parking hassle matters. I don’t want the weekend to start with Mark circling a garage in Santa Fe traffic.

Then Hotel Santa Fe is the calmer choice. It has simpler on-site parking and you are not trying to thread straight into the Plaza core on arrival. Drury is not impossible, but it is more downtown: better once you’re parked, less relaxing while getting there and checking in.
What about the balcony? The Drury balcony room sounds nice, but I don’t need a view. I just don’t want a dark ground-floor room.

At Hotel Santa Fe, I’d treat patio or balcony as a nice-to-have rather than the whole reason to book. The patio king is the safer room-type if you want outdoor space attached. If you book the standard king, add requests for an upper-floor or bright room, away from elevators and service areas, with balcony or patio if available. If they can only place you first floor, a patio room is less disappointing than a generic interior-facing room.
The rate I see right now is $252 refundable for standard king and $275 refundable for patio king. Is the patio worth the extra $69 for the weekend?

For this trip, yes if the $69 stays all-in around that amount. March weather is variable, but the patio gives you a more relaxed room and still keeps the total below the downtown balcony option. If the patio room jumps by more than $100-$125 total, I’d take the standard king and rely on the room request instead.
Okay, let’s do Hotel Santa Fe, refundable patio king if it’s still there. Drury can be the backup if the rate disappears or the hotel can’t confirm amenities.

Good pick. Before you finalize, verify the cancellation deadline, total with taxes and parking, and that the pool, hot tub, and fitness room are operating that weekend. Also check whether the patio king is actually cancellable and not prepaid. If those all check out, book Hotel Santa Fe now and put Drury Plaza on a browser tab only as the fallback.
Should I call before reserving, or book online first and then call?

Book the refundable patio king online first so the rate does not vanish, then call the hotel with the confirmation number. Ask them to note: quiet patio king, not near elevator or service area, bright room if possible, and late-arrival friendly check-in. Confirm parking cost and amenity hours on the call. If the call reveals a surprise fee or closed hot tub, cancel within the window and move to Drury Plaza.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Santa Fe lodging is booked at Hotel Santa Fe with parking and late check-in confirmed. Erin wanted a low-stress weather-aware drive plan and a flexible recovery weekend outline rather than a detailed itinerary.

messages.content: Hotel Santa Fe is booked. Parking and late check-in are confirmed. Now the forecast is showing wind and maybe light snow near the higher stretches on Friday. Can you give me a practical drive-day plan and a loose Saturday plan? Not minute by minute.

Aim to leave Denver around 8:30-9:00 Friday after the morning rush, not early afternoon. Take I-25 south, fuel before Pueblo or Trinidad, and plan lunch around Trinidad or Raton so you cross Raton Pass in daylight. Check COtrip and New Mexico Roads before leaving and again at Trinidad. If there are chain restrictions, high-wind closures, or deteriorating snow on the pass, delay rather than push through. For Friday night, keep dinner low-effort near the Railyard or do a short rideshare into town after you’re settled.
Mark has an 8 a.m. call, so 8:45 is realistic. Leaving at 1 would be a bad idea, right?

I would avoid 1 p.m. for this forecast. That puts the pass and the last northern New Mexico stretch later in the day, when wind and refreeze risk are more annoying. If you cannot leave by late morning, I’d rather wait for a cleaner Saturday morning than turn Friday into a white-knuckle drive.
For Saturday, what’s a light hike that won’t be icy or too exposed?

Pick based on conditions that morning. If it’s dry and mild, do a short lower Dale Ball loop and keep it under 90 minutes. If trails are muddy or icy, choose something sunnier and lower-effort like Galisteo Basin or Cerrillos Hills. If the wind is the problem, skip the hike and do Railyard galleries, the Georgia O’Keeffe Museum, or a soak reservation at Ten Thousand Waves if there’s availability.
Should I book dinner now or keep that flexible too?

Book Saturday dinner now, ideally around 7 p.m., because that’s the night where a plan will make the trip feel intentional. Keep Friday casual and close to the hotel. For Sunday, make an earlier dinner reservation or leave it flexible depending on how much energy you both have.
What’s the last checklist before we leave Denver?

Thursday night: recheck weather, COtrip/NM Roads, tire pressure, wiper fluid, charging cables, meds, and downloaded maps. Friday morning: confirm the hotel has your late-arrival note, screenshot the parking details, pack layers and trail shoes, and recheck Raton Pass before committing past Trinidad. Also save your Saturday dinner reservation and one bad-weather backup so you’re not making decisions in the car.

messages.content: Back to work travel. I need to start the Twin Cities training week, but the client still hasn’t confirmed whether we’re at the Bloomington lab near MSP or the Maple Grove hospital training room. Sessions are Tuesday through Thursday, and there may be a Monday afternoon equipment receipt. Can we build options without assuming the site too early?

Yes. I’d keep the airport fixed as MSP and separate the hotel decision by site. Before I rank anything, what are the travel dates, hotel cap, and how early you’d need to be on site Monday if the equipment receipt happens?

Travel Monday Apr 20, home Thursday Apr 23. Three hotel nights. Cap is $225 before tax. From Denver to MSP. Keep the flight nonstop if it’s reasonable; United or Delta are fine, but schedule matters more. If receipt is confirmed, I need to be at the site by 4 p.m. If not, an afternoon departure is better. For hotels, I’d like 4.0 or better if possible, and pool/hot tub/gym would be useful after training days.

That points to two flight tracks. If the 4 p.m. equipment receipt is real, take a morning nonstop: Delta around 10:10 a.m. arriving MSP about 1:05 p.m. is the safer choice because it leaves time for bags, rental car, and traffic. If the receipt drops, a United nonstop around 1:30 p.m. arriving about 4:25 p.m. is cleaner for your day. For Thursday, I’d look at a nonstop after 6 p.m. unless the client confirms a hard early wrap.
Can you rank the hotel pairings by possible site? I don’t want to commute from the wrong side of town for three mornings.

If Bloomington is confirmed, first hold Hilton Garden Inn Minneapolis Airport/Mall of America: typically under cap, about 4.2 guest rating, pool, hot tub, and fitness, with a short drive to MSP-area labs. Second would be Hyatt Regency Bloomington-Minneapolis: often a nicer room product and about 4.4, good fitness and pool, but the hot tub is less certain. If Maple Grove is confirmed, first hold Cambria Hotel Minneapolis Maple Grove: about 4.4, usually near the cap, pool/hot tub/fitness, and much closer to the hospital training rooms. Second is Courtyard Maple Grove/Arbor Lakes: about 4.3 and convenient, but check the hot tub before relying on it.
Which pair is safest if they drag their feet for another week?

Flight can wait a little because MSP is the airport either way, but hotels should be protected. If your travel system allows no-deposit refundable holds, hold one Bloomington room and one Maple Grove room for 48 hours, then release the wrong one as soon as the client answers. I would not book one central compromise hotel; it would give you mediocre commutes to both places.
I can double-hold hotels for 48 hours. Which exact two would you hold?

Hold Hilton Garden Inn Airport/Mall of America for Bloomington and Cambria Maple Grove for the hospital option. Both are under the cap in the rate range you described, both are well reviewed, and both are more likely to cover pool, hot tub, and fitness than the alternates. Use cancellable rates only, and verify parking fees because Maple Grove is usually easier there than the airport/MOA area.
How ugly is the Maple Grove commute from MSP if there’s weather?

In normal traffic, MSP to Maple Grove is roughly 35-45 minutes. In rain, late snow, or rush hour, it can become 55-70. Bloomington is much lower-risk because you’re staying close to both the airport and likely lab area. If Maple Grove is the site and equipment receipt is at 4 p.m., do not plan around a 1:30 arrival; take the 10:10 Delta and rent a car.
So if equipment is at 4, Delta morning nonstop. If no equipment, United afternoon nonstop. Is that the clean decision?

Yes. For a firm 4 p.m. receipt, choose the 10:10 a.m. Delta nonstop so delays and rental-car pickup do not wreck the first task. If Monday is only a travel day, choose the 1:30 p.m. United nonstop. For Thursday, use the 6:15-ish nonstop if sessions end by 3 p.m.; use the later 7:40-ish nonstop if there is any chance of wrap-up or equipment repack running long.
What exactly should I ask the client before I book?

Ask for five confirmations: the final training address, whether Monday equipment receipt is required and at what time, whether there is secure storage after receipt, the Thursday end time including repack, and whether parking or rental car costs are reimbursable for the Maple Grove scenario. Once they answer, book the matching hotel, release the other hold, then ticket the nonstop flight that fits the Monday equipment decision.
